solution.description: The point is given in polar form, so record the radius r as 4 and the angle theta as 32 degrees before doing any calculation.
Recall the two conversion formulas that will be used: the x-coordinate is r times cosine theta, and the y-coordinate is r times sine theta.
Substitute r = 4 and theta = 32 degrees into the x formula, leaving the cosine unevaluated for the moment.
Evaluate the cosine of 32 degrees, about 0.8480, with the calculator in degree mode.
Multiply the radius 4 by 0.8480 to finish the x-coordinate, 3.392.
Set up the y-coordinate the same way, substituting r = 4 and theta = 32 degrees into the y formula.
Evaluate the sine of 32 degrees, about 0.5299, again in degree mode.
Multiply the radius 4 by 0.5299 to finish the y-coordinate, 2.1196.
Round both coordinates to two decimal places, giving x about 3.39 and y about 2.12.
Substitute r = 6 and theta = 137 degrees into the x formula to set up the x-coordinate.
Evaluate 6 times the cosine of 137 degrees to get x = -4.388; the value is negative because 137 degrees lies in the second quadrant, where x is negative.
Set up the y-coordinate by substituting the same radius and angle into y = r sine theta.
Evaluate 6 times the sine of 137 degrees to get y = 4.092, which is positive because sine stays positive in the second quadrant.
Substitute r = 4.5 and theta = 5.16 into the x formula; because the angle is in radians, put the calculator into radian mode first.
Evaluate 4.5 times the cosine of 5.16 radians to get x = 1.948.
Set up the y-coordinate with the same radius and the same radian angle.
Evaluate 4.5 times the sine of 5.16 radians to get y = -4.057; 5.16 radians lands in the fourth quadrant, where sine is negative.
Sketch the point at radius 4 and 32 degrees so you can see which quadrant it falls in and check the signs of the answers later.
Substitute r = 4 and theta = 32 degrees into x = r cosine theta and evaluate to get the x-coordinate, 3.39.
Substitute the same radius and angle into y = r sine theta and evaluate to get the y-coordinate, 2.12.
Sketch the point at radius 6 and 137 degrees; it lies in the second quadrant, which warns you in advance that the x-coordinate will come out negative.
Substitute r = 6 and theta = 137 degrees into the x formula and evaluate, giving x = -4.388.
Substitute the same values into the y formula and evaluate, giving y = 4.092.
Sketch the point at radius 4.5 and an angle of 5.16 radians, a little over three quarters of a turn, so the expected signs of x and y are clear.
Substitute r = 4.5 and theta = 5.16 radians into the x formula and evaluate, giving x = 1.948.
Substitute the same values into the y formula and evaluate, giving y = -4.057.

Cost is the carpet actually bought, not the bare floor, so multiply 24.375 square metres by the price of 16.80 pounds per square metre.
Carry out that multiplication to get 409.50 pounds.
Round to the nearest pound as the question asks, so 409.50 pounds becomes 410 pounds.

solution.description: A scale of 1 to 250 means each millimetre on the plan stands for 250 millimetres of real garage, so the scale is the ratio of drawing length to actual length.

Multiply 5 by 2.5 to get the true area, 12.5 square metres.
